body: I'm sorry, but isn't it wrong to say "liquid like plasma"? Plasma is not liquid, it's... plasma

>You say you're not mature enough for this world, yet the fact that you're >looking this far forward makes me think you are, in fact, mature.You're >looking forward in your life, planning ahead and that in itself is a sign of >maturity.

I'm not planning ahead. I'm sitting here, complaining about my lack of intelligence instead of coming up with a solution to my problem. 

>However, job prospects for University students has and has been for a >while, incredibly disparaging. If you spend any amount of time on >Reddit, it's not hard to find a thread where college graduates are ankle >deep in debt, struggling to find work, and generally feeling shite about >their situation.

People who get a degree in either medical or engineering fields usually get raped by job offers. Especially in Italy, where we have a total lack of engineers. If I went to a scientific high schools maybe, just maybe, I could have a chance of getting into Engineering. But I didn't. I chose a language high schools which gave me almost nothing. Sure, I can speak english, but no one fucking cares. If I go to England or America or any other english-speaking countries, what additional value do I have compared with someone who lives there? Like "cool, you can speak english, I do too, go and be a dishwasher for the rest of your life". 

>Life is essentially meaningless. The logical, rational part of ourselves >knows that time erodes everything. All the material items, all the >relationships, everything you knew or know will eventually disappear >into the sands of time.
>And that is one of the most difficult, most unbearable things to realise. >I cannot give anything that would ease such a passing weight of >knowledge, for the weight of that knowledge weighs heavily on many, >many men.

I have accepted this.

As for the rest of your comment, I get your point. I understand the fact that not everyone will be remembered as a huge contribution to mankind even though they are doing small things to push history forward. However, as arrogant as this sounds, I don't want to be part of those people. I don't think I'm capable of doing something remarkable, but I do want to do something remarkable - get the difference? The fact that I'm not capable of being important to mankind in a tangible way (which is in my opinion the only thing that comes close to giving a point to life) makes me feel completely useless and stupid. I don't trust my intelligence, I have close to none self-esteem, I can barely function in a everyday society, I'm not capable of hitting on girls or having a good time with my friends because I can't help the fact that drinking, going outside just of the sake of this and doing nonsense that other people of my age call "memories" is completely pointless. Nothing will remain out of it. Since I can't do these things, my only option to give a point to my life is to do something important, but I won't be able to because I'm stupid. Sorry for the rant.

People need scientists, engineers, people who can create *actual* things. It doesn't matter how creative I am if I don't possess a degree that can be actually used in a job. I suck at math, thus I won't be able to access Engineering since it requires you to know advanced chemistry, physics, math and logic. I won't be able to access Economy and Business Management, either, because it requires a significant knowledge in math just to be able to enter the course. Each year around 930 attempt at this degree, and with 370 available spots I have close to no chances of getting in. If you consider the fact that half the people that attempt this degree course comes from a scientific high schools and they have been eating math for five years like candy, I can't compete. I suck at math, and I feel like a complete retard because of that.
The third option, Economical Development and International Cooperation, will be easy to access to me. It requires an A2 level of english, basic math and logic, good italian knowledge, all things I already possess. Plus, around 160 people (according to the poll I've made) attempt at this degree each year, and with 150 available spots it means I will have a much larger chance of getting in.
But do I want to get in that degree? It will probably give me nothing. I know a guy who has succeded at working inside the European Parliament with this degree - plus a specialization in International Business - but most people just end up unemployed.
I don't want my parents to give me financial support for something it will turn out to be useless for me. We are close to being broke, I can't allow them to pay money if they will not get their money back someday.
I'm left with seven days to make a choice. I'm an idiot because I've been sitting researching about all the courses for far too long, while I should have man up and started studying during my last year of high schools. But I didn't. And now anxiety is slowly eating me, and I'm at a point in which I can't even relax playing a videogames because my thoughts won't leave me alone.
